name: Disposition Evaluation Criteria
description: How the District decides whether a property should be sold or transferred. A higher result means a stronger case for disposition.

criteria.label: Loss of program alignment
criteria.description: Extent to which the property no longer serves an adopted District program.

criteria.label: Management cost burden
criteria.description: Cost and effort of continuing to hold and maintain the property.

criteria.label: Isolation from other holdings
criteria.description: Whether the property stands alone, away from other District land.

criteria.label: Remaining resource value
criteria.description: Habitat or resource value still present. Higher score = less value remaining.

criteria.label: Realisable value
criteria.description: Proceeds the District could reasonably expect from a sale or exchange.

criteria.label: Public interest in retention
criteria.description: Community use or attachment. Higher score = less public interest in keeping it.

criteria.label: Freedom from legal constraint
criteria.description: Absence of deed restrictions, grant conditions or reversionary interests. Higher score = fewer constraints.
